comment: I use a permit nearby. yes to excluding these addresses, though i doubt it fixes parking on its own
why should someone in the new building get different rules than me? I live nearby and disagree with the exclusion.
no car so not a big issue for me. still want the housing
YES. there cannot be an endless queue of cars for the same bit of curb. support the exclusion
Looking at places around here... would want to figure out transit and parking before deciding on this one.
Have a permit myself, still seems unfair to the new neighbours.
I work on Dundas and favour this. Customers parking is a different question tho
Not sure. I work here but the notice doesnt really tell me what changes day to day.
Transit most days for me. Im fine with these buildings being outside the permit area.
i take transit too, that doesnt mean nobody needs a car. dont like excluding an entire address
visiting friends, no real opinion
I would rather have one consistent approach for older and newer buildings. Hard to defend the difference just from the address.
I live nearby and honestly cant place parts 1 and 2. need the highlighted map before i have an opinion
Fine with closing the listed pieces.
Prefer keeping the road land as it is. I know this isnt the whole of Lawrence closing.
neutral. looks like a boundary thing?
I go through here regularly. The street names got my attention but I cannot work out whether these two pieces affect my route. A map would help.
yes for the portions in the notice, not voting to close the street!
I work nearby. Once road land is closed thats a big commitment to me... not sure if our access is even involved but I lean against it.
only here sometimes, dont know enough
No strong citywide opinion on two little parcels.
good to have a name for it. Aren Levy Lane works for me
its a lane. as long as i can explain where it is to someone im good either way
Who is the name recognising? not against it, just dont know yet.
Could we name it after where it IS instead? I dont want giving directions to turn into a local history exam lol. prefer a location name
I work around here, a name would make directions easier.
no preference really
pass Vaughan often. havent spent much time thinking about the lane name tbh
I like named lanes. easier to point to a place than say the little lane behind that other place
Yes please. This building is part of what makes the area feel like Weston to me.
The roof is the interesting bit for me, plus the recreation history. support designation
I want flexibility to change the building later. worried designation makes that harder so its a no from me
what does this mean for normal repairs? genuine question, undecided
usable recreation space first for me. neutral about the designation itself
I visit for recreation and like that the inside counts too, not just the front of the building.
Glad the skating history gets recognised. Not reading this as a promise of new programs or anything.
My priority is being able to improve the facility. I dont want the answer to every new idea being "but heritage". against designation
I work in Weston. Keeping a recognisable community building seems worthwhile.
The history is interesting but I have no idea what the obligations would be. unsure
PLEASE keep the timber roof. Toronto does not need to turn every interesting interior into the same white box.
drive past, dont use it. no strong view
Overall yes to the mixed use building. Removing the heritage bit bothers me more than the alterations do. Definitely keep the conservation plan requirement.
46 storeys?? we can add housing without making every building look like it is trying to win a height competition. against this, still want a conservation plan
Yes to the building and the heritage approach in the notice. We need room for more people.
I cant picture the old and new parts together. happy they need a relocation/conservation plan but undecided on the approval
leave the heritage attribute where it is. A plan is important but it doesnt undo removing the thing in the first place
I work close by. More people and different uses could be good for the area; support the approvals with the conservation planning.
The scale is too much for me and I worry about disruption at work. Havent seen enough of the conservation details to rate those.
no overall vote either way yet. dont like the removal, do like having a proper plan
I pass through regularly, more homes sounds good. Neutral on the attribute removal, yes to the conservation plan.
i like seeing the older parts of the street when i visit. losing an original piece still feels like a loss, plan or no plan
need drawings. what stays, what moves? cannot visualise this
Support. New housing and the heritage measures described here seem like a workable combination.
Would rather keep the heritage attribute in its setting. Conservation planning matters, I just disagree with this approval.
lean yes overall. Not sure about that specific removal - i understand they arent talking about knocking down everything on the property
Use this route, support the temporary bridge then the permanent one. Record the old one properly too.
replacement makes sense. not enough info for me to say yes or no to demolition
I want the replacement route but im not sold on removing the old bridge. those are different questions to me
Get on with the bridge plan please! support it, including documenting the old structure and looking at salvage.
Replacement plus remembering what was here seems a fair balance.
I live nearby and would rather keep the old bridge. Still favour the temporary/replacement planning if this goes ahead.
how temporary is temporary?? would like to know before picking a side. yes to recording the history
No. I like THIS bridge, not a brand new bridge with a plaque saying there used to be a nice bridge here. Still document it carefully.
i visit for walks etc. fine with a replacement and recording the history, no strong demolition opinion
The old bridge is part of why i enjoy coming here. against taking it down, havent decided about the new design
neutral for now... need to see what the replacement would look like. documentation is a good idea
Work takes me this way. support the bridge plan but the timing is still a question for me.
A sign is not a bridge! I oppose demolition even though the replacement route could be useful. Please do the recording and salvage review.
Support the replacement and commemoration. Would be nice to use old pieces where possible, know that isnt guaranteed.
